hook: A porcelain theatre mask that wants to be worn is a classic horror image, and this file uses it well. The mask talks, flatters and bargains, so the real threat is persuasion rather than force. Expect suicides, killings and blood-soaked ritual imagery in the later addenda, all logged in flat report style.
whyItMatters: It is an early Keter that is dangerous mostly because it is charming: the most important containment rule is about who is allowed to talk to it. The comedy-and-tragedy mask, the possession idea and a containment log that keeps getting worse make it one of the easiest files to picture and to remember.
thingsToNotice:
Wearing the mask kills the wearer outright: its mind overwrites theirs, the brain dies, and the body rots into a mummified husk that the mask keeps puppeting long after it should be able to move. In conversation it is brilliant and friendly, yet it talks some interviewers into suicide and others into mindless servitude, and it later turns out to read minds without any host at all.

The addenda are a slow losing battle. Staff help it try to escape and are executed; when command bans new hosts, some personnel turn violent and everyone who had contact is terminated again. Then the cell walls start bleeding contaminated human blood that forms texts in old languages and diagrams of sacrifices resembling staff and their families, and the translation team dies in a mass suicide and killing. Lining the walls with another anomaly calms the rest of the site but traps everything inside, until the room is soaked in blood, hands reach out of puddles, and the file ends by suggesting the whole cell may simply have to be abandoned.

related.note: Named as one of the bodies the mask wants; staff fear its regeneration would make a permanent host.
The material used to line the cell, which shields the site but seals the dread inside.
